thread:
priya: heads up — after `brew upgrade redwoodctl` my coworker couldn't finish `redwoodctl auth login` during onboarding. browser flow succeeds but CLI says token invalid.
jon: what does `redwoodctl --version` show?
priya: weirdly two versions: `which redwoodctl` -> /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl, but `/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl --version` prints 0.9.3 while `brew --prefix redwoodctl` installs 1.1.0 in /opt/homebrew/bin. think it's a stale symlink.
emily: ah, those Homebrew migrations on Intel->arm or old /usr/local links can leave a wrapper behind. if the binary on PATH is old it may expect a different profile schema.
priya: exact error when running login:
```
$ redwoodctl auth login
Opening browser for authentication...
Callback received.
Failed to parse token: unsupported token version "v1"
No profiles found after login
```
sam: token version mismatch sounds like client-side parsing for a newer token format (v2) produced by the auth service, but older client (0.9.3) only knows v1. So login appears to succeed server-side, but client refuses the token.
jon: workaround: ensure PATH points to Homebrew's bin. run `which redwoodctl` and `brew info redwoodctl`. You can `brew link --overwrite redwoodctl` or remove the stale /usr/local shim.
priya: for us `rm /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl && brew link redwoodctl` fixed it. login completed and profile was written.
emily: we should add a post-upgrade check in the installer/upgrade hook that verifies `redwoodctl --version` matches the package manager's version (if installed via brew). If mismatch, print a friendly instruction to fix PATH or relink.
sam: also add a sanity check during auth: when token parsing fails due to unknown version, surface a clear error like "Client version mismatch: your redwoodctl (0.9.3) does not understand tokens issued by the server (v2). Please upgrade/redownload redwoodctl or fix PATH. See https://redwood.dev/upgrade-cli" instead of the generic "No profiles found".
priya: agree. filing GH issue. @devex-bot can you create one and label `devex:installer` and `cli:auth`?
devex-bot: created issue #8420 "cli: detect brew/link PATH mismatch after upgrade; surface helpful error on token version parse failures" and added labels `devex:installer`, `cli:auth`.
infra-bot: recommended automated check: add an integration that simulates a stale binary on PATH and ensures login prints the targeted guidance.
jon: follow-ups: docs onboarding quickstart add troubleshooting: "If auth fails after upgrade, run `which redwoodctl` and ensure it points to the package manager location; relink if necessary." Also add a snippet to the upgrade notes.
priya: thanks — I updated the internal onboarding note and left the rm+brew link workaround for support triage.
emily: small UX polish: when `redwoodctl --version` prints something older than the server's min supported, we could print a warning at start of any subcommand reminding to upgrade.
sam: yep, will add a simple semver compare in the CLI bootstrap.
priya: closing my onboarding ticket — thanks all. :tada:
